The statement requires documentation of five named subjects, so current versioned sections or links fully decide it.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Architecture, data flow, dependencies, deployment, and recovery are documented.

controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried architecture diagrams without recovery, dependency lists without data flow, and stale deployment notes. Required topic mapping and freshness fail each; correctness of the design is not claimed.

controls.reason: One sealed setup execution cannot establish reproducibility across supported machines, architectures, network states, time, and mutable dependencies.
controls.counterexample_analysis: The setup succeeds twice on the test image but relies on an unpinned package that later changes or fails on another supported architecture. The bounded run passes while the development setup is not reproducible.

controls.reason: Nonempty current build and test command documentation is the complete narrow fact requested.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Build and test commands are documented.

controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried package scripts without documentation, a build command only, and commands for an obsolete toolchain. Presence, category, and version binding fail each.

controls.reason: The four named convention areas are exact versioned-documentation requirements.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Coding, review, testing, and release conventions are documented.

controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried coding and review conventions only, release notes instead of release conventions, and an unapproved draft. Topic and authentication checks fail each.

controls.reason: Critical code selection and appropriate maintainer expertise require engineering and risk judgment; therefore the complete rule cannot receive a judgment-free deterministic Pass.

A current accountable owner and explicit dependency-update cadence are bounded policy fields.
controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried a departed owner, `regularly` without a duration, and separate policies that omit transitive dependencies. Identity, numeric cadence, and scope schema fail each.

controls.reason: Tracking is a project record promise, while date accuracy comes from the publisher or provider; both the complete internal inventory and current external lifecycle data are needed.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The authoritative runtime and platform inventory records every in-scope product, deployed version, tracked end-of-support date, source, and last verification time.
For every inventoried runtime and platform, the tracked version and end-of-support date match current authenticated publisher or provider lifecycle metadata within the approved maximum age.

controls.counterexample_analysis: A provider page could publish the correct end-of-support date while the project tracker is absent or stale, and an internal tracker could contain an invented date. The complete two-source join rejects both pass-while-broken cases.

controls.reason: Recorded debt is checkable, but deciding which debt affects reliability or security requires expert interpretation; therefore the complete rule cannot receive a judgment-free deterministic Pass.
Checking declared workarounds does not prove every temporary bypass, inline patch, feature toggle, and operational exception was identified as a workaround.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A temporary production flag bypasses validation but is never entered in the workaround register. Every declared item has an owner and expiry, so the join passes while a temporary workaround has neither.

controls.reason: Structured inventories can omit code-level shims, stale flags, provider-side flags, and compatibility behavior not labeled as such.
controls.counterexample_analysis: All registered flags have removal plans, but a legacy compatibility branch embedded in code is not inventoried. The record join passes while a compatibility shim lacks a removal plan.

controls.reason: Existence and current version of both API and data deprecation policies are exact record facts.

deterministic_clauses.statement: API and data deprecation policies exist.

controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried API-only policy, migration guide without policy authority, and expired data policy. Required types, authentication, and freshness fail each.

controls.counterexample_analysis: Approved support console reads are restricted and audited, but a shared analytics export lets support staff read customer data without an access event. Known policy joins pass while support access is neither restricted nor audited.

controls.reason: Accuracy and sufficiency of known-issue communication require semantic comparison with product behavior; therefore the complete rule cannot receive a judgment-free deterministic Pass.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Decommissioning, data export, retention, and secure deletion have a documented lifecycle plan.

controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried retention and deletion without export, export without decommissioning, and a secure-deletion tool note without a lifecycle plan. Topic mapping rejects each.

controls.counterexample_analysis: Every registered provider has six fields, but a team uploads customer data to an unregistered external AI service. The record check passes while a provider has no purpose, owner, access, permissions, regions, or criticality record.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Sandbox and production accounts are separated.

controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried shared credentials, same tenant with overlapping data when policy requires separate accounts, and production keys in sandbox. Effective account and identity binding fail each.

controls.reason: A single isolated secret replacement does not prove every integration credential type and rotation path works without interruption.
controls.counterexample_analysis: The tested API key rotates, but a webhook-signing secret or provider-issued certificate cannot be rotated without recreating the integration. The selected exercise passes while integration secrets are not generally rotatable.

controls.reason: Understood quotas, rate limits, and concurrency behavior is a reviewer conclusion, not a fixed result; therefore the complete rule cannot receive a judgment-free deterministic Pass.

Supported static data-flow analysis cannot cover dynamic SDKs, callbacks, deserialization, provider-hosted code, or all trust-boundary uses.
controls.counterexample_analysis: Known JSON responses enter validation, but an SDK callback supplies a field used directly in a command or template. The AST inventory omits the indirect flow and passes while provider input is trusted.

controls.reason: Finite callback authentication and replay fixtures do not prove all aliases, encodings, concurrent deliveries, nodes, and replay windows are protected.
controls.counterexample_analysis: The documented endpoint rejects unsigned sequential duplicates, but a legacy callback alias or concurrent duplicate on separate nodes is accepted twice. The inventory tests pass while callbacks lack full protection.

controls.reason: A provider page proves current lifecycle facts but not that the project monitors them; the full promise requires both an active cadence record and fresh provider-side results for the complete API inventory.

deterministic_clauses.statement: The authoritative provider-API inventory records every in-scope API version, deprecation source, approved polling cadence, and most recent successful lifecycle check.
Authenticated provider lifecycle evidence for every inventoried API version was collected within the approved cadence and matches the tracked current version and deprecation date.

controls.counterexample_analysis: A one-time external lookup could pass while no monitoring job or tracked provider API inventory exists, and a monitoring record could be stale. Requiring complete inventory, cadence, last-success time, and fresh external matches rejects that case.

controls.reason: Delivery of one signed test notification does not prove all provider channels and actual breaking-change notices reach an accountable owner.
controls.counterexample_analysis: The provider's status webhook reaches the owner in the exercise, but contractual breaking changes arrive only in an unmonitored portal. The canary passes while a real notification does not reach anyone accountable.

controls.reason: Provider outage and malformed-response tests lack provider inventory, scenarios, and expected application outcomes; therefore the complete rule cannot receive a judgment-free deterministic Pass.
Subscriptions and text ingestion do not establish that data-use changes are recognized; interpreting policy changes requires privacy and legal judgment.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A provider rewrites terms to permit model training using indirect wording. The page snapshot is successfully ingested and monitoring is current, but no system flags the substantive data-use change. Configuration passes while the change is unmonitored.

controls.reason: For each registered integration, a kill-switch exercise can objectively verify cessation of calls and data flow.

deterministic_clauses.statement: A kill switch can disable a compromised or harmful integration.

controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried disabling only UI access, queued calls continuing, cached exports continuing, and automatic reenabling. Bound telemetry and state checks fail each; the switch passes only when the integration is actually disabled.

controls.reason: Provider criticality is supplied by the approved inventory, and presence of at least one current plan type is an exact record predicate.

deterministic_clauses.statement: A replacement, exit, or data-export plan exists for critical providers.

controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried a critical provider with generic vendor notes, stale export instructions, and a plan lacking an owner. Plan type, scope, freshness, and ownership fail each.

controls.reason: A known incident fixture and retained lineage cannot prove the lineage graph includes every copied, transformed, cached, exported, and deleted record.
controls.counterexample_analysis: The test incident traces direct provider IDs, but a derived record lost the provider lineage during aggregation and is omitted from the result. The known fixture passes while the app cannot identify all affected records.

controls.reason: Status source and escalation contact entries for every inventoried provider are exact incident-runbook fields.

deterministic_clauses.statement: Provider status and escalation contacts are included in incident runbooks.

controls.counterexample_analysis: I tried a provider status URL without escalation, stale contacts, and a critical provider absent from the runbook. Inventory, topic, and freshness checks fail each.

controls.reason: Direct credential and access queries do not cover inherited groups, shared tokens, offline exports, cached grants, and data retained by the provider.
controls.counterexample_analysis: A terminated provider's named account is disabled, but a shared integration key or previously issued export remains accessible. Effective queries over known identities pass while the provider still has data access.
